title: Inquest probes fatal Brantford police shooting
article: An inquest has been called to probe the death of a Brantford teen who was shot dead in his home by a Brantford police officer last August.
Evan Jones was shot inside home in a townhouse complex on Sympatica Crescent on the city's northeast side at 9:50 p.m. on Aug. 25 during a confrontation with police.
Dr. Bonita Porter, Deputy Chief Coroner for Inquests, said in a statement Thursday the inquest will be held June 21 at the Brantford courthouse.
The Ontario Special Investigations unit which investigated the death found no fault on the part of the police officer who fired the fatal shot.
The investigation found police encountered Jones on the front porch of the townhouse holding two large knives.

The officer who was deemed subject of the investigation, drew his firearm and told Jones to drop the knives several times but Jones held the blades to his throat and demanded that the police kill him. Then he went back into his house.
Police learned Jones's sister and 2-year-old niece were inside and two officers went inside as another officer went in the back door.
Once inside they found Jones with the two knives and he refused to drop them. As Jones advanced on the two officers who had come in the front door he was pepper sprayed without effect.

At that point Jones raised the knives and threw one of them at the two officers and turned with a meat cleaver raised over his head in the direction where the subject officer had reason to believe another officer was situated.
The subject officer fired multiple shots, hitting Jones four times. The youth was pronounced dead at the scene.
The SIU concluded the officer used lethal force to prevent an imminent, potentially lethal, attack against another police officer.
An inquest is mandatory under the Coroners Act.

Dr. Jack Stanborough will preside over the inquest which is expected to last four days. It will examine the events surrounding Jones' death and the jury may make recommendations aimed at preventing similar deaths.
The inquest will begin at 9 a.m. on Tuesday, June 21, at the Brantford courthouse.
